summary: Sol Runner: Grand Tour is an interactive space-exploration game where players travel from an orbital space station to the Moon, Mars, Europa, and Titan. Players pilot a shuttle, land with a rover, collect and analyze scientific samples, and learn about real planetary environments through NASA-based facts and mission data. The game supports both single-player exploration and online multiplayer co-op, where players can meet at the station and launch shared missions together. It addresses the challenge by transforming real space science into an accessible and engaging experience. The project is important because it encourages curiosity about planetary science, exploration, robotics, and future human missions through interactive gameplay rather than passive information.
details:
Sol Runner: Grand Tour begins in an orbital observation station. Players can explore the station, interact with the command center, use the space shuttle to travel between destinations, and select missions from a solar-system map. After landing, they drive a rover across the surface, search for scientific samples, manage battery power, and return before environmental conditions or mission limits end the expedition.

Collected samples can be analyzed to reveal scientific information and links to NASA resources. The game also includes realistic concepts such as gravity, distance, sunlight, temperature, daylight duration, weather reports, and communication delays.

The project was developed using TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Three.js, Vite, WebSockets, and Cloudflare Durable Objects. It is deployed publicly through Cloudflare Workers, with GitHub used for source control. The multiplayer system allows players to create or join rooms and participate in cooperative missions.

The project is creative because it combines education, exploration, simulation, and multiplayer interaction in a game inspired by real space missions. Design decisions considered accessibility, clear controls, scientific accuracy, performance, responsive visuals, reliable networking, and making complex space concepts understandable for a general audience.
